purpose: Hydrochlorothiazide is used to treat high blood pressure and to reduce fluid buildup (swelling) in the body caused by conditions like heart failure or kidney problems. Lowering high blood pressure helps protect you from heart attacks, strokes, and kidney damage. It may be used alone or combined with other blood pressure medications.
how_it_works: This medicine works by telling your kidneys to remove extra salt and water from your body through your urine. Because there is less fluid in your blood vessels, your blood pressure goes down. Think of it like relieving pressure in an overfilled water balloon by letting some water out.
common_side_effects: You may need to urinate more often, especially when you first start taking it. Other common side effects include dizziness, feeling lightheaded when you stand up quickly, muscle cramps, feeling thirsty, and low potassium levels. Sensitivity to sunlight can also increase, so use sunscreen when outdoors.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to sulfa drugs, as you may also be allergic to this medicine. This medication can lower potassium levels in your blood, so your doctor may recommend eating potassium-rich foods like bananas or may prescribe a supplement. Avoid drinking alcohol as it can worsen dizziness. Tell your doctor if you have diabetes, gout, or kidney or liver problems before taking this medication. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The typical starting dose for adults is 12.5 mg to 25 mg taken once daily in the morning. Your doctor may increase the dose up to 50 mg per day depending on how your body responds. Taking it in the morning helps prevent having to wake up at night to urinate. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes.
